findings.title: Egress gate does not prove that Anthropic receives the scrubbed payload
findings.where: scripts/check-llm-egress.mjs:125; scripts/check-llm-egress.mjs:128; scripts/check-llm-egress.mjs:154; scripts/check-llm-egress.mjs:165; scripts/check-llm-egress.test.mjs:77; scripts/check-llm-egress.test.mjs:123
findings.what: validateLlmWrapperCallSites reduces all calls to two registry-ID sets. Any egressScrub('id', ...) anywhere in the registered file satisfies the scrub requirement for callAnthropic('id', sensitivePayload), even if the scrub result is discarded, occurs in dead code, or scrubs a different value. Consequently this release gate can pass while ~/.claude-derived content is sent under subscription OAuth credentials, contrary to the stated egress boundary.
findings.fix: Make the approved send API accept only an opaque value returned by egressScrub, or extend the AST validation to require each protected wrapper payload argument to be data-flow-linked to a same-ID scrub result. Add a negative test where a scrub result is discarded and an unrelated payload is sent.
findings.acceptance: A fixture containing `egressScrub('server.fake', safeValue, options); callAnthropicMessages('server.fake', sensitiveValue);` must be rejected, while sending the captured same-ID scrub result must pass.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that collection records only file, line, callee, and registryId (lines 92-123), while validation stores only registry IDs in independent sets (lines 125-169). The tests at lines 77-155 exercise discovery and presence but contain no payload-flow assertion; therefore the bypass is reproducible from the audited logic and is not merely a missing-style check.
